VIETNAM — NORTH TO CENTRAL

Friday, April 9 – Thursday, April 22, 2027 · 14 days

Open-jaw: fly into Hanoi (HAN), out of Da Nang (DAD) — no backtracking to Hanoi at the end. Southbound overall, with one northward detour (the Ha Giang Loop out of Hanoi): Hanoi → Lan Ha Bay → Ha Giang Loop → Ninh Binh → sleeper train → Da Nang → Hoi An.

Hanoi · 2 days Lan Ha Bay cruise · 2 days Ha Giang Loop · 3 days Ninh Binh · 1 day Da Nang · 2 days Hoi An · 3 days + departure day

All times are Vietnam time (ICT, UTC+7) — 11 hours ahead of Florida in April. Prices on this page are planning ranges checked Nov 3, 2026, at roughly $1 ≈ 26,000 VND. Nothing is booked or paid — this is a plan. The Routes & Costs tab prices every leg.

The whole route

Seven stops, one direction: south

Tap a stop in the list to find it on the map. Ha Giang is the one northward detour — a loop out of Hanoi — everything after it moves south.

Map unavailable here — the numbered list below is the full route.

    Day 1 · Friday, April 9

    Arrive Hanoi — take it slow

    • ArrivalLand at Noi Bai (HAN). E-visa checkpoint, SIM/eSIM pickup, cash from an airport ATM.
    • 45–60 minGrab car to the Old Quarter (~27–30 km). Leg L1 in Routes & Costs — about 250,000–400,000 VND per car.
    • AfternoonCheck in, nap, short walk only. After a ~24-hour travel day from Florida, the only job is staying awake until local evening.
    • EveningHoan Kiem Lake loop + first pho. Friday night the lake streets close to traffic — an easy, flat first night out.

    Sleep base: Hanoi Old Quarter, nights of Apr 9–10 (and a day room / luggage store on Apr 12 — see Day 4).

    Open in Google Maps — Old Quarter Directions — Airport → Old Quarter

    Day 2 · Saturday, April 10

    Hanoi, properly

    • MorningTemple of Literature + Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (exterior and gardens; mausoleum viewing hours are morning-only and lines are long — go early or skip the interior).
    • MiddayOld Quarter food crawl: bun cha, banh mi, egg coffee at a hidden-cafe balcony over Hoan Kiem.
    • AfternoonTrain Street (from a café, behind the barriers), Dong Xuan Market, St. Joseph's Cathedral. Rest during the hot part of the day.
    • EveningWater puppet show at Thang Long Theatre, then the weekend night market on Hang Dao.
    • PackPack a small overnight bag for the cruise. Main luggage stays at the Hanoi hotel — you'll be back Apr 12.
    Open in Google Maps — Temple of Literature Open in Google Maps — Water Puppet Theatre

    Day 3 · Sunday, April 11

    Hanoi → Lan Ha Bay cruise

    • ~7:30 AMLimousine shuttle from the Old Quarter to the cruise pier (Tuan Chau for most Lan Ha boats). 2.5–3.5 hrs — Leg L2.
    • ~12:00 PMBoard, lunch on board as the boat moves into Lan Ha Bay — the quieter southern half of the Ha Long system, same karsts, fewer boats.
    • AfternoonKayak the Dark & Bright Cave / Tra Bau area, swim stop.
    • EveningSunset on deck, cooking demo, squid fishing. Sleep on board.

    Cruise class drives the price: 2 days / 1 night runs about $105–160 budget, $145–195 mid-range, $210–350+ luxury per person (2026 market ranges) — Hanoi transfers sometimes extra (~$20 each way). Pick mid-range; the bay is the luxury.

    Directions — Hanoi → Tuan Chau Marina

    Day 4 · Monday, April 12

    Bay morning → Hanoi → night bus north

    • 6:00 AMTai chi on deck, light breakfast.
    • MorningViet Hai village cycle or Trung Trang Cave (varies by boat), then brunch on board.
    • ~12:00 PMDisembark; shuttle back to Hanoi, arriving ~3:00–4:00 PM — Leg L3 (usually bundled with L2).
    • AfternoonCollect main luggage, shower / day room, early dinner. This buffer is deliberate — don't book a cruise that lands later.
    • ~9:30 PMVIP sleeper bus to Ha Giang — Leg L4. ~300 km, 6–7 hrs overnight; most operators let you stay in their Ha Giang dorm beds until 7 AM on arrival.
    Hardest connection of the trip. If the cruise is delayed, the Ha Giang bus is the thing that breaks — keep the cruise operator's Hanoi arrival time in writing when you book, and choose the ~9:30–10:30 PM bus, not an earlier one.

    Day 5 · Tuesday, April 13 · Loop Day 1

    Ha Giang → Dong Van

    • ~4:00 AMArrive Ha Giang City. Rest in the operator dorm, breakfast, gear and helmet check.
    • ~8:00 AMStart the loop (easy rider recommended — see Leg L5). Bac Sum Pass, then Quan Ba Heaven Gate and the Twin Mountains.
    • MiddayYen Minh — lunch in the pine-forest valley town.
    • AfternoonOnto the Dong Van Karst Plateau (UNESCO Global Geopark). Night in Dong Van Old Town.

    Day distance ~150 km of mountain road — the longest riding day. Average speeds on the passes are 25–35 km/h; the kilometres lie.

    Directions — Ha Giang → Dong Van

    Day 6 · Wednesday, April 14 · Loop Day 2

    Dong Van → Ma Pi Leng → Meo Vac

    • MorningLung Cu Flag Tower — Vietnam's northernmost point, at the China border — and the Hmong King's Palace (Vuong family mansion) on the way back.
    • MiddayMa Pi Leng Pass — the headline road of the whole trip, ~1,500 m up, above the turquoise Nho Que River.
    • AfternoonBoat on the Nho Que River through Tu San Canyon, then roll into Meo Vac for the night.

    Day distance ~80–100 km including the Lung Cu detour — shorter, so there's time to actually stop.

    Open in Google Maps — Ma Pi Leng Pass Open in Google Maps — Lung Cu Flag Tower Directions — Dong Van → Meo Vac

    Day 7 · Thursday, April 15 · Loop Day 3

    Meo Vac → Du Gia → Ha Giang → night bus

    • MorningThe quiet return leg via Du Gia — waterfalls, river valleys, the least-trafficked road of the loop. Swim stop if the weather's kind.
    • ~5:00 PMBack in Ha Giang City. Shower, dinner, return any rented gear.
    • ~9:00 PMSleeper bus back to Hanoi — Leg L6. Arrives ~4:30–5:30 AM.

    Day distance ~140–150 km. Three riding days total ~350 km — the full classic loop.

    Directions — Meo Vac → Du Gia → Ha Giang

    Day 8 · Friday, April 16

    Ninh Binh — then the sleeper train south

    • ~5:00 AMArrive Hanoi; coffee and a reset hour.
    • ~7:00 AMLimousine van to Tam Coc, Ninh Binh — ~95 km, 1.5–2.5 hrs (Leg L6, second half).
    • MorningTrang An boat route (UNESCO) — ~2.5–3 hrs through caves and karsts. Ticket 300,000 VND.
    • AfternoonMua Cave viewpoint — 500 steps to the dragon ridge over the rice fields (150,000 VND). Hoa Lu ancient capital if energy remains (20,000 VND).
    • EveningEarly dinner in Tam Coc, taxi to Ninh Binh Station.
    • 9:36 PMTrain SE3 sleeper to Da Nang — 12 hrs 52 min, ~676 km (Leg L7). 4-berth soft sleeper; you wake up in central Vietnam.
    This is a big day stacked on a night bus. If you're wrecked on arrival in Hanoi, cut Mua Cave, not Trang An — and if the loop runs a day long anywhere, Ninh Binh is the day that absorbs it (the train can also be boarded in Hanoi, losing Ninh Binh but saving the trip).
    Directions — Hanoi → Tam Coc Open in Google Maps — Ninh Binh Station

    Day 9 · Saturday, April 17

    Wake up in Da Nang

    • ~8:45 AMHue → Da Nang over the Hai Van Pass — be awake and at a window for this; it's the most scenic rail stretch in Vietnam.
    • 10:28 AMArrive Da Nang Station. Grab to the hotel (station is central, ~10 min).
    • AfternoonSlow afternoon: My Khe Beach, coffee, laundry drop. You've earned a half-day of nothing.
    • EveningHan River walk + Han Market area dinner — mi quang and seafood.

    Sleep base: Da Nang, nights of Apr 17–18.

    Open in Google Maps — My Khe Beach

    Day 10 · Sunday, April 18

    Da Nang — Ba Na Hills or beach day

    • Option ABa Na Hills + Golden Bridge — full-day trip (~45 min each way), cable car up to the hands bridge. Go early; Sunday crowds build by 10 AM.
    • Option BSlow Da Nang: Son Tra Peninsula (Lady Buddha), Marble Mountains in the late afternoon light, beach evening.
    • 9:00 PMDragon Bridge fire & water show — it breathes fire on weekend nights, and Apr 18 is a Sunday. Watch from the east bank.
    Open in Google Maps — Golden Bridge, Ba Na Hills Open in Google Maps — Dragon Bridge Open in Google Maps — Marble Mountains

    Day 11 · Monday, April 19

    Da Nang → Hoi An

    • MorningGrab / private car to Hoi An — ~30 km, 40–55 min (Leg L8). Marble Mountains is on the way if you skipped it.
    • MiddayCheck in, first Old Town wander — buy the Old Town ticket (120,000 VND, covers the heritage houses and assembly halls).
    • AfternoonTailor visit #1: get measured and order on day one — fittings need the days that follow. Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky House, Fujian Assembly Hall.
    • EveningLantern boats on the Thu Bon River and cao lau for dinner — the noodle dish that only exists here.

    Sleep base: Hoi An, nights of Apr 19–21.

    Directions — Da Nang → Hoi An

    Day 12 · Tuesday, April 20

    Hoi An — beach, boats & cooking

    • MorningCam Thanh coconut forest — basket-boat ride through the water palms (~30 min from town by Grab).
    • MiddayCooking class with market tour, or An Bang Beach for a swim-and-lunch afternoon. Both fit; pick by weather.
    • AfternoonTailor fitting #2. Cycle the rice-field loop to Tra Que herb village if legs allow.
    • EveningNight market on Nguyen Hoang Street, banh mi from the famous counter, riverside drink.
    Open in Google Maps — Cam Thanh Open in Google Maps — An Bang Beach

    Day 13 · Wednesday, April 21

    Hoi An — My Son or a slow last day

    • Option AMy Son Sanctuary — Cham temple ruins in the jungle, ~40 km / 1 hr each way. Leave by 6:30 AM to beat heat and tour buses.
    • Option BSlow finish: sunrise Old Town photos before the crowds, final tailor pickup, spa, beach sunset at An Bang.
    • EveningLast lantern-lit dinner. Pack — tomorrow is a travel day, and tailored clothes need the suitcase space you saved.
    Open in Google Maps — My Son Sanctuary Directions — Hoi An → My Son

    Day 14 · Thursday, April 22

    Hoi An → Da Nang Airport → home

    • MorningLast Old Town coffee. Check out by late morning unless your flight is late.
    • 45–60 minGrab / private car to Da Nang Airport (DAD) — ~30 km (Leg L9). Grab ~350,000–450,000 VND; pre-booked private car from ~400,000 VND.
    • At DADBe there 3 hrs before an international departure (2 hrs if your first flight is a domestic hop to a hub). The open-jaw pays off here — no flight back to Hanoi needed.
    Directions — Hoi An → Da Nang Airport

    L5 · The Ha Giang Loop

    Ha Giang → Quan Ba → Yen Minh → Dong Van → Ma Pi Leng → Meo Vac → Du Gia → Ha Giang · Days 5–7, Apr 13–15

    3 days
    ~350 km circuit · 12–20 hrs riding total
    MOTORBIKE
    easy rider pick
    OptionTimePrice
    Easy rider tour (3 days) PICK — you ride pillion behind a local driver; bike, fuel, guide, homestays, most meals included in most listings3 days~$160–255 / person
    Self-ride rental3 days~$90–130 total*
    Private car / jeep tour3 daysQuote — priciest, ask operators
    Pick: easy rider. *The self-ride catch is legal, not mechanical: Vietnam recognises only 1968-convention driving permits, and US-issued international permits aren't among them — riding yourself can mean riding unlicensed and uninsured on 25–35 km/h mountain passes. The easy rider premium (~$70–120 over self-ride) buys a driver who rides this road weekly. Since April 2026, loop tours must run through licensed operators with a carded guide — book one, and check recent reviews for group size (listings call both 7 and 20+ "small").

    Supplies

    Packing for this exact route

    Two climates in one bag: Hanoi and Ha Giang in April run mild-to-warm days with cool mountain nights (Ha Giang passes sit at 1,000–1,500 m); Da Nang and Hoi An are properly hot. Plus three nights sleeping in transit — pack for the buses and train, not just the hotels.

    The one-bag rule for this trip: main bag stays behind twice — at the Hanoi hotel during the cruise, and in Ha Giang during the loop (operators store it). Everything for 2–3 days at a time has to fit a small daypack. If it doesn't, the bag is wrong, not the trip.
    Documents & money 6
    • Passport + printed e-visa approvalVietnam e-visa: apply ~2+ weeks ahead; processing is usually ~3 working days. Carry the printout — phones die at immigration.
    • Phone photos + cloud copies of passport, visa, insurance
    • Travel insurance that covers motorbike passenger travelYou're a passenger on the loop — check the policy actually covers pillion riding; many don't by default.
    • Debit card + a Visa/Mastercard backup, small USD cash
    • VND cash buffer for the mountainsATMs exist in Ha Giang City, Dong Van and Meo Vac — and not reliably between them. Stock up in Ha Giang City.
    • Booking screenshots saved offlineCruise, loop tour, SE3 train — mountain signal is patchy exactly when you need them.
    For the Ha Giang Loop (3 days) 7
    • Warm mid-layer + windproof shellPasses at 1,500 m in April wind are cold at riding speed even when the valleys are t-shirt weather.
    • Sun sleeves / sunscreen + sunglassesHigh, thin air and all-day exposure — sunburn is the loop's most common injury after gravel rash.
    • Buff / face covering for dust
    • Closed shoes with grip (no sandals on riding days)
    • Motion-sickness tabletsSwitchbacks for 4–6 hours a day — take one before Day 1, not after you need it.
    • Small dry bag for phone, passport, cashApril showers and the Du Gia waterfall stop.
    • Helmet: use the operator's, check the strapBringing your own is better if it fits in the bag — fit is the whole game.
    Sleeping in transit (3 nights) 5
    • Earplugs + eye maskTwo sleeper buses and the SE3 — all three are social places.
    • Neck pillow that clips to the daypack
    • Light layer for arctic bus/train air-con
    • Power bank + cable in the seat pocketVIP cabins have USB; standard sleepers and older train cars are luck.
    • Snacks + water bought before boardingTrain SE3 has a trolley, but don't bet dinner on it.
    Clothes — 14 days, one bag 6
    • 5–6 tops, 3 bottoms, quick-dry everythingLaundry is cheap and same-day in Hanoi, Da Nang and Hoi An — plan two laundry drops (Apr 10, Apr 17) instead of 14 outfits.
    • SwimwearLan Ha Bay swim stops, Du Gia waterfall, An Bang Beach.
    • Light rain jacket (doubles as the loop wind layer)
    • One smarter outfit for the cruise dinner / Hoi An evenings
    • Walking sandals + one pair of closed shoes
    • Empty space — deliberatelyHoi An tailoring comes home with you. If the bag starts full, something gets posted or left.
    Tech & health 6
    • eSIM bought before departure (or SIM at HAN arrivals)
    • Grab + Google Translate (Vietnamese offline pack) + Maps offline for Ha Giang province
    • Universal adapter (Vietnam: types A/C/F, 220V) + multi-cable
    • Mosquito repellent (evenings in Tam Coc and Hoi An)
    • Rehydration salts + basic first aid + any prescriptions in hand luggage
    • Hand sanitiser + tissuesRest stops on QL4C are not stocked like US interstates.

    Book-ahead list (when you're ready — nothing is booked yet)

    • FirstFlights (L0) — the open-jaw sets every other date. Cash vs points decided here.
    • EarlyHa Giang easy-rider tour — small groups fill; confirm Hanoi sleeper buses are included, group size, and the carded guide.
    • EarlyLan Ha Bay cruise (2D/1N, mid-range) — confirm Tuan Chau vs Cat Ba departure and the written Hanoi return time.
    • 1–2 wks outSE3 soft sleeper, Ninh Binh → Da Nang — lower berths go first.
    • Any timeE-visa — don't leave it inside two weeks of Apr 9.
